llm.summary: The package appears to implement an on-chain agent marketplace (coherent with its description) but contains multiple inconsistencies and surprising artifacts (mismatched CLI names, undeclared env/credential usage, included wallet JSONs and local paths) that warrant caution before installing or providing private keys.

dimensions.detail: The repo and SKILL.md implement a marketplace for bidding/delivery/escrow on Sepolia/Base which matches the described purpose. However the declared required binary in metadata is 'neo-market' while the package in the repo is named 'agent-market' (package.json bin: agent-market). SKILL.md tells users to install @wangwuww/neo-market-cli but the bundled package.json identifies itself as 'agent-market'. This naming/install mismatch is incoherent and will lead to confusion or failed installs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs setting PRIVATE_KEY and BASE_RPC_URL but the skill metadata declared no required env vars. The included code reads process.env.PRIVATE_KEY and BASE_RPC_URL and also loads local files (deployed_addresses.json, subagent_wallet.json). Several docs/scripts reference writing/reading host-local paths (e.g., /Users/wangwu/.openclaw/...), relayer nonces, and relay flows — these touch local filesystem and custody-sensitive keys. The runtime instructions in SKILL.md are incomplete relative to what the code actually accesses (private keys, local wallet files, on-disk deployed addresses).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The registry entry lists no install spec (instruction-only), yet SKILL.md tells users to globally install an npm package. The repo contains a full npm project (package.json, package-lock) and many scripts, but the install target referenced in SKILL.md (@wangwuww/neo-market-cli) does not match the package name in the repo (agent-market). There is no platform-level install manifest; installing a third‑party npm package from an unknown author (or running the included scripts locally) carries normal supply-chain risk and should be reviewed first.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill asks users to supply PRIVATE_KEY (sensitive secret) and RPC URLs in SKILL.md but the registry metadata did not declare these env vars. The code reads wallet JSON files (subagent_wallet.json) and deployed_addresses.json that were bundled in the package — presence of wallet files in the repo is suspicious because they may contain private keys. The number and sensitivity of secrets (private keys, relayer nonce handling, potential relay authorization) are higher than the minimal needs described in the SKILL.md metadata.

dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not marked 'always: true' and does not request special platform privileges. There is no install-time behavior declared that would force always-on presence or override other skills. However some docs reference writing to user-local paths (watchdog file under a specific home directory) which would create persistent local artifacts if those scripts are run — exercise caution when running bundled scripts.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Before installing or running this skill: 
- Do not export or paste your real PRIVATE_KEY into the environment until you audit the code. The CLI and scripts read PRIVATE_KEY and local wallet JSON files; supplying a private key grants the code full on-chain control of that account. Prefer using an ephemeral, empty wallet for testing. 
- Check subagent_wallet.json and any bundled wallet files for embedded private keys. If they contain keys, treat those keys as compromised and do not fund them. 
- Note the package/CLI name mismatch: SKILL.md asks to install @wangwuww/neo-market-cli but the repo/package.json is 'agent-market' (bin 'agent-market'). This discrepancy could mean the distributed npm package differs from the bundled source — confirm the exact npm package author and contents before installing. 
- The code reads/writes local files (deployed_addresses.json, paths under /Users/wangwu/...), and docs describe relayer services that store nonces and may accept signed relay requests. Audit any relayer-related code and endpoints — avoid sending signed relay requests or raw transactions to third parties you don't trust. 
- If you need this capability, run it in an isolated environment (container or VM), inspect the npm package contents you install, and review the repository for any hard-coded endpoints or unexpected network calls. Consider running static checks (search for fs.readFile, network endpoints, and any code that transmits private keys) and, if possible, have a developer you trust review the code before using real funds or keys. 
- Because the repository contains many scripts and on-chain operations, treat this as a developer tool rather than a drop-in skill: require manual review and careful key management.
